issues.legal_issue: An assessment made after a partnership has been dissolved is invalid when it is made against the non-existing firm without notice to the interested partner, and notice to another former partner does not suffice.
material_facts: The firm had been dissolved before the assessment was made.
The assessment was made against the dissolved firm.
Notice of the assessment proceedings was given to one former partner, but not to the deceased partner whose liability was asserted.
The tax authority refused the widow’s request for a clearance certificate on the basis of the alleged arrears.
issues.conclusion: There was no valid assessment on the deceased partner. The widow was therefore not liable to discharge the alleged tax liability, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: After a partnership has been dissolved, a former partner cannot be treated as the other partner’s agent for the purpose of an income-tax assessment. Notice to that former partner is not notice to the interested partner. An assessment made against a non-existing firm without notice to the interested person is invalid. The judgment identifies no earlier cases or statutory provision as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.assessment_proceeding_after_partnership_: A tax assessment proceeding was conducted after the partnership had been dissolved.
predicates.assessment_made_against_nonexistent_firm: The assessment was made against the firm even though it no longer existed.
predicates.interested_partner_received_no_notice: The partner whose liability was asserted was not given notice of the assessment proceeding.
predicates.notice_given_only_to_another_former_part: Notice of the assessment proceeding was given only to another former partner.

issues.definition: When an assessment proceeding occurs after a partnership is dissolved, the assessment is made against the non-existing firm, the interested partner receives no notice, and notice is given only to another former partner, the assessment is invalid.
